question: Did Peña have a conflict of interest over Ueno?

sideA.label: Impeachment accusers
sideA.text: Peña was a business partner of Grupo Vázquez until 2025, took two simultaneous Ueno loans, appointed an ex-Ueno head to the Central Bank and favoured Ueno at IPS.

sideB.label: Peña / Ueno
sideB.text: The bank says he was never a shareholder or investor, and Peña said the concerns were exaggerated by the media and belong with the courts.

resolution: Senate removed him 44-0 for mal desempeño; no court has ruled on the criminal allegations.

question: Was Peña removed or did he resign?

sideA.label: Resignation account
sideA.text: Early reports, including CNN Español, said Peña resigned on 5 Nov.

sideB.label: Removal account
sideB.text: Congress never voted on the resignation for lack of quorum, and the Senate removed him on 6 Nov.

resolution: Removal by the Senate is the better supported account (La Nación, La República, BBC Mundo).

question: Was Peña arrested?

sideA.label: Detention reports
sideA.text: La Nación's live blog reports house arrest ordered at about 22:42 and transfer to the Regimiento Escolta Presidencial; La República carried a "detenido" headline.

sideB.label: Not confirmed
sideB.text: Other outlets reviewed do not report an arrest, and the La República article body does not either.

resolution: Unverified; needs a Ministerio Público statement.

sideA.label: Central Bank
sideA.text: Solvency fell below 50% of the legal minimum after adjustments to its financial statements during regularization.

sideB.label: Critics
sideB.text: Excess lending to owner-linked firms and heavy public-fund deposits point to governance failure and state capture.

question: How did deputies vote on impeachment?

sideA.label: La Nación
sideA.text: 78 legislators present approved the accusation, including all Colorado members.

sideB.label: Other report
sideB.text: A separate piece cited 48 against and 30 in favor but appears to refer to Alliana.

resolution: Official Chamber tally not yet verified.
